tools.name: Blender
tools.note: A food processor can be used in its place.

tools.name: Saucepan
tools.note: Use a small saucepan, which is the size the eggs need.

tools.name: Pot
tools.note: Use a large, heavy pot so the paste and broth cook evenly.

tools.name: Serving bowl
tools.note: Four deep serving bowls are listed in the recipe, so any bowls of similar depth will do.

steps.title: Prep the aromatics and chicken
points: Prepare everything before you turn on the stove.
Cut off the tough tops and root ends of the lemongrass, peel away the dry outer layer, and slice the pale lower part thinly.
Roughly chop the chilies (remove the seeds for a milder soup), shallots, garlic, and peeled ginger.
Put these in the blender with the coriander, cumin, turmeric, 2 tablespoons of the oil, and 2 to 3 tablespoons of water, and blend to a smooth paste.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Rinse the bean sprouts, pick the cilantro leaves from the stems, and cut the limes into wedges.

steps.title: Boil and chill eggs
points: Bring the small saucepan of water to a boil over high heat.
Lower in the eggs with the slotted spoon, reduce to a steady simmer, and cook for 9 minutes.
Move them to the ice water for 5 minutes, then peel and halve them.

steps.title: Fry the paste
points: Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in the large heavy pot over medium-low heat.
Add the paste and fry it for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often with the wooden spoon, until it darkens, smells fragrant rather than raw, and the oil begins to separate from it.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken in coconut broth
points: Stir in the stock, coconut milk, fish sauce, and brown sugar.
Raise the heat to medium and bring to a gentle simmer, with small bubbles only.
Add the chicken and simmer for 15 minutes, until it is cooked through with no pink in the middle.

steps.title: Blanch sprouts and cook noodles
points: While the chicken simmers, bring the medium pot of water to a boil over high heat.
Blanch the bean sprouts for 30 seconds and lift them out with the slotted spoon.
Add the noodles to the same water and cook according to the package, usually 3 to 5 minutes, until just tender.
Drain them in the colander, rinse briefly under warm water, and divide among the serving bowls.

steps.title: Simmer the shrimp
points: Add the shrimp to the broth and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
Taste and add more fish sauce if it needs salt, or a squeeze from one lime wedge if it needs brightness.

steps.title: Assemble and serve the bowls
points: Ladle the broth, chicken, and shrimp over the noodles.
Top each bowl with bean sprouts, two egg halves, and cilantro, and serve with the remaining lime wedges.

troubleshooting.problem: The broth tastes harsh or raw
troubleshooting.solution: The paste was not fried long enough. Next time keep it on medium-low until it darkens and the oil separates, which takes the full 8 to 10 minutes.

troubleshooting.problem: The broth looks grainy or oily on top
troubleshooting.solution: The coconut milk boiled too hard and split. Keep it at a gentle simmer once the coconut milk goes in.

troubleshooting.problem: The noodles turn soft and swollen
troubleshooting.solution: They sat in the broth too long. Cook them in their own pot and put them in the bowls only just before serving.
The chili seeds carry most of the heat. Seed the chilies next time, and for now stir in a little extra coconut milk or stock.
